question.text: A biased coin with probability $p(0 \lt p \lt 1)$ of getting head is tossed until a head appears for the first time. If the probability that the number of tosses required is even is $\frac{2}{5}$, then $p=$

solution.text:
Hint: required probability will be
$\begin{aligned}
& (1-p) p+(1-p)^3 p+\cdots \infty=\frac{2}{5} \\
& \Rightarrow p\left[\frac{1-p}{1-(1-p)^2}\right]=\frac{2}{5} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{p(1-p)}{1-\left(1-2 p+p^2\right)}=\frac{2}{5} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{p-p^2}{2 p-p^2}=\frac{2}{5} \\
& \Rightarrow p=\frac{1}{3}
\end{aligned}$
